io.github.captainssingapura-hue.homing.js:homing-workspace-shell 0.4.0 发布, Universal workspace chrome substrate — the orchestrator and its
        sub-classes that every WorkspaceShell-derived AppModule shares.

        Born from a refactor: prior to this module, the entire workspace
        boot sequence (WorkspaceLayout mount, MTP wiring, picker plumbing,
        persistence attach, identity resolution, event-log + replay,
        checkpoint store, Web Lock + read-only fence) lived as ~2,100 lines
        of JS-as-Java-string-literals inside per-workspace chrome widgets
        (e.g. AnimalsPlaygroundChrome.bodyJs() in homing-demo). This
        module promotes that mass into proper ES modules — one class per
        responsibility, each independently testable.

        Doctrines made concrete:

        - Modest File Size: every class sits comfortably under the cap.
        - Generated and Hand-Written Live Apart: JS lives in .js files,
          not Java string-literal lists.
        - Functional Objects: each JS class has explicit state, pure
          behaviour, inspect() output (extended from the Java doctrine).
        - Diligent Secretaries: every component is testable in isolation
          via the GraalVM harness without a DOM.

        Position in the dep graph: sits above homing-workspace-persistence
        (the highest workspace utility module) so it can compose every
        substrate piece below.

io.github.captainssingapura-hue.homing.js:homing-ssjs-test-fixtures 0.4.0 发布, Test fixtures for pure-JavaScript code authored under the homing
        ssjs (server-side-JS) substrate.

        Vends a GraalVM-Polyglot-backed JUnit harness so any pure JS module
        — Secretaries (RFC 0028), client-side reducers, validators,
        serialisation helpers — can be unit-tested on the JVM against a real
        ECMAScript runtime, without spinning up a browser or transpiling.

        The harness is split into two layers:

          - JsModuleTestBase — generic. Boots a JS context, loads a module
            from the classpath, looks up named exports, ships an envelope()
            helper that marshals Java Maps into native JS objects via
            ProxyObject, and tears the context down on @AfterEach.

          - SecretaryTestBase — Diligent-Secretaries-doctrine layer. Adds
            the Step contract — initial(), dispatch(state, env) — and terse
            assertions over { newState, actions }.

        Dependencies (GraalVM Polyglot + js-community) are exposed at
        compile scope intentionally: this module IS test fixtures, so a
        downstream test module pulling it in (typically at test scope from
        its own pom) automatically gets a working runtime with no further
        config.

        Public downstream projects can depend on this module identically to
        any homing artifact; the test-fixtures naming makes the intent
        legible at the dependency-graph level (vs. opaque test-jar
        classifiers, which the dependency-as-test-jar refactor explicitly
        replaced).

io.github.captainssingapura-hue.homing.js:homing-workspace 0.4.0 发布, RFC 0025 — Workspace + Dynamic Widget Management. A strict downstream
        of homing-studio-base providing the workspace shell pattern: a
        per-page registry of WorkspaceWidget types, a controller that
        dynamically loads modules on user pick, a picker UI, and the
        WorkspaceShell AppModule base that ties it together.

        Studios that don't need workspace capabilities (catalogue browsers,
        doc readers, single-widget viewers) leave this dependency off and pay
        nothing for the machinery. Studios that want workspace add this dep.

        The WorkspaceWidget contract is distinct from RFC 0024's Widget — see
        the Rfc0025Ext1Doc for the design and the rationale. Both contracts
        coexist; a WorkspaceWidget can be hosted in a non-workspace context
        by wrapping it in a degenerate mini-workspace (one widget, no picker,
        no layout management).

io.github.captainssingapura-hue.homing.js:homing-codec 0.4.0 发布, Meta-Function ontology — the higher-level interface layer that names
        the typed objects involved in moving data across language seams via
        generated code rather than runtime reflection.

        Four ontology objects:

        1. ObjectDefinition<T> — typed source-of-truth
        2. TransformationFunctions<T, W> — pure encode/decode pair
        3. FunctionsCodeGen — produces source code of TransformationFunctions
        4. DefinitionCodeGen — translates ObjectDefinition across languages

        Pure-interface module — no implementations. Concrete codecs live
        with their Value Objects in the modules that own those records
        (Names Are Types in action: each Object Definition's codec is
        co-located with the Object Definition itself).

        Doctrinal anchor: CodeGen as Functions. Hand-written, automated,
        and AI-assisted implementations all conform to the same interface;
        provenance is invisible at the contract boundary.

        Deferred: a Java-side JSON parser (for the day data flows back
        from JS to Java). Not needed yet — only Java→JS direction is in
        scope for the early consumers.

io.github.captainssingapura-hue.homing.js:homing-tree-views 0.4.0 发布, Rigid tree substrate — typed leveled TreeNode value objects + a
        canonical JSON serialiser that becomes the universal contract for
        rendering any tree-shaped artifact on JS without a single line of
        per-tree-kind JS code.

        Borrows DomOpsParty's leveled-types pattern: TreeLevel is a sealed
        sum (L0..L8); TreeNode<L extends TreeLevel> is parameterised on
        its depth. Per-tree-kind adapter records (in studio-base and
        downstream modules) map native shapes (catalogues, ComposedDoc
        segments, future tree-shaped doc kinds) to TreeNode<L> — a
        thin String-to-typed-wrapping boundary.

        Substrate vocabulary:
        - Dimension(key, value)      — typed metadata pair
        - DimensionKey               — sealed; small substrate vocabulary
        - DimensionValue             — non-sealed; extension point
        - DisplayLabel / LevelDepth  — bundled DimensionKey constants
        - NameValue / DepthValue     — bundled DimensionValue records
        - TreeNodeJsonWriter         — canonical JSON serialiser

        Doctrinal anchors: Names Are Types (no raw strings on the contract
        surface), Make It Impossible Not Forbidden (level type enforces
        per-depth shape), One Stone Two Birds (substrate consolidation +
        future pivot/grid/outline transforms compound on the same shape).
